title: The Last Message
summary: The two personalities left on the universe’s final archive planet face their last choice between humanity’s memories and the possibility of new life.
content:
The child spoke, dividing the breath into thirteen parts.

[Mom, I was here.]

Miriam-17 turned off the audio and poured tea into a white cup. The blue fish at the bottom of the cup sank into the 43-degree water.

There were no stars outside the window. Only the archive planet revolved around the last artificial black hole. Beneath the ice sea, 80 quintillion records slept, from love letters to the history of planets.

Sophia-0 pushed the cup away.

“Now that all the stars are gone, do we still have to watch the tea’s temperature?”

“It’s the temperature Noah liked.”

“So we’re using the universe’s last electricity on a dead person’s taste.”

“If you lose even their taste, all that remains of the record is a list of names.”

[Remaining life: 17 days]

Sophia tapped the extinguished star chart.

“If we burn all the records, we can open a seed for a new universe.”

“Where?”

“Not in any direction in this universe. If we compress the planet’s mass and the black hole’s rotation into a single point and create a false-vacuum bubble, it will hang from our spacetime by a slender neck.”

“Do we send the seed through that neck?”

“No. Once expansion begins, the neck breaks. One black hole closes for us, but inside it, space opens and time takes its first step.”

“Then humanity dies twice.”

“If there’s no one to read it, a record is only a tomb.”

“A tomb is an empty room too, until someone finds it.”

Around 100 trillion years into the universe’s age, the last naturally born child was born. Her mother showed her the blue sea and named her Noah. Not a name meaning survive, but a name meaning leave a place to rest for someone who would cross over.

Time passed after that. The age of stars and black holes had passed as well. Time was counted only by the final rotations of the underground machines.

A black sphere rose from the center of the planet. Each time the 42 scars on its surface contracted thirteen times, one storage layer went dark.

[Estimated transmission time: after the end of the current universe]
[Sentence deciphered: 92%]

The first three left a difference between matter and antimatter, and the remaining 39 separated them again whenever they were erased. From that gap, stars and seas and humans were born.

“It didn’t come from the past.”

“Then who sent it?”

“Someone who would be born after us. A receiver who hadn’t arrived yet answered first.”

Sophia placed her hand on the sphere.

“Then let’s send something too.”

Miriam stepped in front of her.

“Who gave you the right to burn 80 quintillion memories?”

“Then who gave you the right to decide the answer of something that hasn’t even been born?”

[Mutual refusal]
[Remaining life: 108 seconds]
[Final mediation record revealed]

The seal opened.

[Preserved personality: Miriam-17]
[Inherited personality: Sophia-0]
[Common original: Noah]

The first video played again.

[Mom, I was here.]

It was a recording left by six-year-old Noah for her hibernating mother. As an adult, Noah had divided her mind in two so that she could not decide humanity’s final meaning alone. The part that waited became Miriam. The part that spoke first became Sophia.

They bent the same finger at the same time.

“If you hadn’t been here, I would have put Noah’s name in a coffin and carried it into the next universe.”

“If you hadn’t been here, I would have burned Noah and called it freedom.”

[Remaining life: 42 seconds]

The commotion of humanity came alive again in Noah’s memories. Humans made vessels that would last. They left names to their children, years to their schools, and trademarks to their companies. Religions carried the voices of the dead into prayer, and nations carried yesterday’s promises into tomorrow.

People believed they had placed eternity in those vessels. They built castles, rang bells, loved, fought, and died. But children lived differently, and schools revised what they taught. Companies and nations rose and fell, and prayers were read differently too. What remained was a trace shaped by the next person.

As the storage layers collapsed, names filled the black sky. Golden liquid flowed through every crack in the ice continent. Preserved memories became water again.

“If we send it as it is, the next life will be trapped in our past.”

“If we erase it all, even what we received from them ends here.”

“Then what do we leave behind?”

“Our names?”

“Names demand to be remembered.”

“A message telling them not to hurt one another?”

“Life also eats and pushes other life away. We can’t leave a lie as a final testament.”

“The answers we learned?”

“Answers take away the next being’s time.”

Sophia deleted the nouns from the civilization records. Human, love, peace, salvation. Miriam deleted the adjectives. Good, eternal, right. Finally, they deleted even the subject. As long as ‘we’ remained, it was a request, not a testimony.

They discarded the memories and kept only the power to pass something on. A golden spiral, a blue pulse that leapt first, an empty ring open to the next being. There were no names, faces, or lessons.

“Only two verbs remain.”

Sophia gazed at the deciphered original for a long time.

“It’s like the sentence we made.”

“No. The sentence we were trying to make came from over there first.”

They created thousands of different versions. Turned into a command, it demanded obedience. Turned into a prayer, it demanded faith. Given a name, it demanded remembrance. In the end, Sophia closed every draft.

“Let’s send it as it is.”

“Then who wrote this sentence first?”

“What matters isn’t who came first, but who comes next.”

They erased the original’s two verbs from speech and writing, and folded them into the interval between two pulses. In the seed’s vacuum, only a minute phase difference remained instead of meaning.

Then one of the black sphere’s sealed scars opened.

[Sentence deciphered: 100%]
[Original locked: to be revealed upon successful transmission]

The final 8 percent was not text but a condition. The sentence would reveal itself only when someone passed it on to the next.

The 80 quintillion records opened. First steps and first kisses, funeral songs and the smell of rain in ruined cities slipped out of the letters and became light. The light drew a round door in the middle of the darkness.

At the end, only the white cup remained. They drank half the tea each and placed their hands on either side of the seed.

“What if no one receives it?”

“We didn’t receive ours because we were someone’s intended recipient either.”

[Transmission failed]
[No recipient]
[3]

The continent folded like a flower petal.

[2]

The white cup melted. Only the blue fish swam against the waves of light for a moment.

[1]

They did not take their hands away.

[0]

The planet disappeared. The forgotten names became round doors, and the empty places of beings not yet born held the center.

Just before the screen went dark, a line that had not existed appeared.

[External pulse detected: 2]

Beyond the darkness, a new space drew its first breath. Light poured out, and time began to run. Dust became stars, and the ashes of stars became blue planets. Rain that fell for eons spread the first sea.

Beneath the light of dawn, two different molecules met. One remembered its shape, and the other made a new shape out of everything it touched. When one trembled first, the other answered in a slightly different rhythm. Between those misaligned answers, a transparent membrane formed.

After twelve pulses, the waves tore the membrane apart. The moment the two moved away from each other, a third beat that belonged to neither rang out from the empty space between them.

It was the thirteenth pulse.

The third beat called the scattering two back together. The membrane closed, wider than before, and the first life raised itself.

A golden spiral unwound inside it. Life reproduced, ate, took, and sometimes lived together. Countless species were born, pushed out other species, and disappeared. What had been passed on was neither goodness nor peace. It was only the direction of something that had survived, trying not to end with itself.

That direction passed through cells and bodies. Some left children, some songs, and some handprints on ruins. What the next being would make of what it received was theirs to decide.

They knew nothing of Noah, Miriam, or Sophia. No one remembered them. And yet, in the transmission record of the archive planet from long ago, one word was erased.

[No recipient]

No one was not a lack, but a place where something not yet given a name could remain.

[Recipient born]

Beneath the dawn sea, the first life moved its tail. It moved in the same direction as the blue fish in the white cup. Its movement overlapped with the phase difference between the two pulses. The moment what had been received passed into the next cell, the original that had arrived first from the future into the past opened.

[If you received it, send it on.]
